\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
The 0xFFFFFFFF of a counter that went below zero is -1 in two's complement: the bits did not change, the reading did. Next: fractions on a chip with no floating-point unit.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item The byte 0xF6 is in memory. Which 32-bit value does lb leave in a register, and which does lbu leave? Which is right if the byte is a temperature of -10 degrees?
\item On 8 bits, compute 0111 1111 + 0000 0001. Read the result as an unsigned number and as a two's-complement number. Is there overflow in each reading?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
